items.term: zero conditional (if you heat ice, it melts)
items.es: condicional cero: si + presente, presente (verdades generales)

example.en: If you heat ice, it melts.

items.term: first conditional for real plans (if it rains, we'll stay in)
items.es: primer condicional: si + presente, will + verbo (algo posible)

example.en: If it rains, we'll stay in.
example.es: Si llueve, nos quedamos en casa.

items.term: second conditional for imaginary situations (if I had…, I would…)
items.es: segundo condicional: si + pasado, would + verbo (algo imaginario)

example.en: If I had a car, I would drive to work.
example.es: Si tuviera auto, iría al trabajo manejando.

items.term: third conditional for past regrets (if I had left earlier…)
items.es: tercer condicional: si + had + participio, would have + participio

example.en: If I had left earlier, I wouldn't have missed the bus.
example.es: Si hubiera salido antes, no habría perdido el autobús.

items.es: unless: a menos que (= if… not)

example.en: I won't go unless you come with me.
example.es: No voy a ir a menos que vengas conmigo.

items.term: if or when (if I see him / when I see him)
items.es: if o when: si (quizás) o cuando (seguro)

example.en: I'll call you when I get home.
example.es: Te llamo cuando llegue a casa.

options: If you heat ice, it melted.

If you heat ice, it melts.

passages.title: What if?
passages.text: My grandfather always says that if he hadn't missed his bus in 1970, he would never have met my grandmother. She was waiting at the same bus stop, and they started talking. 'If I had caught that bus, none of you would be here,' he tells us. My little sister likes to ask him what he would do if he won the lottery. 'If I won a million dollars, I would buy a boat and travel around the world,' he answers. Then he always adds, 'But if your grandmother comes with me, she'll want to drive the boat!'
